text: A2: Room mirror — LWW clock entities, DAOs, repos

23/23 unit tests green (debug + release variants), 0 lint errors,
assembleDebug clean. Real execution verified, not just compiled.

Design: LwwField -> three concrete embedded types (LwwString,
LwwOptionalString, LwwBoolean) instead of one generic LwwField<T> —
Room/KSP can't process a generic @Embedded class with a nullable type
parameter ("Cannot use unbound properties in entities").

DeviceIdProvider is a temporary in-memory random-UUID Hilt binding;
A3 replaces it with the DataStore-persisted one per Notes.

Environment note for whoever picks up A5 (next Robolectric-heavy
ticket) on this same ARM64 sandbox: Robolectric's native SQLite/
native-runtime loader have no linux/aarch64 build, and transitively
pulls conscrypt 2.5.2 which also predates aarch64. Working pattern
that produces real (non-shadow) SQLite execution: keep
@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class) purely for a working Context,
force testImplementation("org.conscrypt:conscrypt-openjdk-uber:2.6.0"),
and testImplementation("androidx.sqlite:sqlite-bundled-jvm:2.7.0")
(NOT the plain "sqlite-bundled" coordinate — that resolves to the
Android-target variant in an Android module and expects natives
pre-extracted into an APK's jniLibs/, so it won't self-load under a
JVM test), then .setDriver(BundledSQLiteDriver()) on the Room builder.
See app/build.gradle.kts comments for the full story. None of this
should be needed on a normal x86_64 dev/CI machine.
